correctness.rationale: Given the cited 2023 exact duality/congruence theorems, independent Ferrers rectangular blocks classify all WHB operations. Every nonzero block has a connected active support and weight binomial(u+v-2,u-1), so the intersection graph of supports plus uncovered chain positions gives exactly the undirected relation component count and hence Boolean congruence rank. The endpoint sum follows with exact multiplicity. Trailing-zero row and initial-zero column binomial ratios are bounded by exp(-min(s,t)/4); a union bound forces all support prefixes/suffixes longer than half and therefore one component, proving the stated generic simplicity bound. Three independent finite enumerations and direct WHB axiom checks passed via the standalone file verify_congruence.py. Finite checks are supporting evidence, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The relevant 2023 primary paper already supplies WHB duality, congruence/doubly closed-set correspondence, and hence the finite undirected-component interpretation; these are not claimed as new. The finding adds for all products of at least two finite chains a weighted Ferrers endpoint-support polynomial resolving every congruence rank, computable with polynomially many states for fixed factor count, and a uniform quantitative theorem that almost all such expansions are simple as minimum chain length increases. Targeted searches of the primary text, related literature, a published mathematical finding index, and the accessible prior research claims disclosed no equivalent full theorem. Residual alternate-language coverage remains possible.

value.rationale: Congruence rank and simplicity control decomposition of finite nonclassical-logical algebras. The all-size weighted normal form on named nontrivial products of chains computes the full congruence distribution in polynomial time for each fixed factor count, instead of iterating over all operations. The distinct uniform probability bound proves that simplicity is asymptotically generic across these product-chain families. This is a natural structural invariant and an infinite-family classification, not a relabeling of classical Ferrers counts or a single arbitrary finite census.
